deviations.from: The open choice the dispatch and the research artifact left to the author: whether the free-disk figure at line 42 needs the same qualifier as the four-item download sentence.
deviations.why: One qualifier only, beside the four-item list under '## What installing gives you'. Line 42 does not describe a download at all: it states how much free disk Hearth requires and says Hearth checks that space before it starts. That figure is disk_required from crates/hearth-probe/src/plan.rs:237, the two-item total plus a fifth, so it is what the installer's own check enforces and the page reports it accurately as such. Qualifying it would also require a magnitude, and no source supplies one: the omitted engine and Python runtime come to 36,326,051 bytes on macOS, but the voice environment's pip installs at crates/hearth-probe/dictionary.yaml:59-67 carry no recorded size anywhere, so the page cannot say whether the plan's one-fifth headroom absorbs them. A bare warning that the budget is short, with no number, leaves a reader budgeting disk worse off than the accurate figure does. The residual fact is recorded in unresolved[].

deviations.from: The qualifier's placement inside the paragraph, relative to the T1 passage at wiki/installing.md:106-112.
deviations.why: The two qualifying sentences are copied from wiki/installing.md:109-111 unchanged, so the two pages now say this the same way. What differs is that on this page the four-item sentence ends in a colon that introduces the install-tree code block. Keeping one paragraph would have run past 60 words against wiki/style-guide.md's paragraph target, so the sentence was split at 'together.' and the folder clause ('Everything lands in one folder you choose (`~/Hearth` by default):') moved to the end of the new paragraph to keep the colon against the fence. No fact was added or dropped in the split, and the ~/Hearth default is unchanged.

deviations.from: The hearth-style skill's instruction to run scripts/lint_wiki.py and scripts/doc_graph.py.
deviations.why: Neither was run. This session's tool set is Read, Grep, Write and Edit, with no command execution, so the linter could not be invoked. The five mechanical conventions at wiki/developing.md:221-232 were applied by hand to the added prose (no em dashes, no emojis, sentence case headings unchanged, relative links unchanged, American spelling), but that is a manual check and not a linter run.
